messages:
erika: FYI: after yesterday's variant swap (runtime v2.14 -> v2.15) a handful of tenants reported higher p95. Telemetry shows a sustained p95 delta from ~85ms -> ~320ms for medium-length prompts. opening thread to triage. @oncall
max: saw alerts at ~08:42 UTC, p99s also up for same cohorts (spikes to ~1.1s). Canary looked fine, but rollout ramped faster than expected.
priya: curious if this is cold-kv vs runtime scheduling. any pattern by seq_len?
erika: good call — looking at APM: p95 delta is concentrated on requests with seq_len 128-1024, and #tokens>200. Short prompts unaffected. traces show extra queueing inside the runtime scheduling layer before kernel dispatch.
jonathan: paste from trace: 
```
span: runtime.scheduler.enqueue (latency 240ms)
  -> span: runtime.kernel_select (60ms)
  -> span: runtime.exec.dispatch (170ms wait)
```
queue depth metric correlates with a sudden bump in scheduler.backpressure_count after the variant swap.
max: that suggests the new variant's packer/scheduler heuristics are causing head-of-line blocking for mid-length sequences. we changed the "thread_packer_v3" heuristic in 2.15, right?
erika: yes, 2.15 enabled thread_packer_v3 by default in kernel selector. can reproduce locally with synthetic workload: many concurrent x=64 seq_len=512 requests.
priya: can you drop the minimal repro steps here so support/customer teams can try?
erika: repro (local):
```
# run 50 concurrent clients against staging variant v2.15
for i in {1..50}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://staging-infer/redwood/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-medium-v1","prompt":"lorem ipsum","max_tokens":300}' &
done
wait
```
observed p95 ~300ms, p99 ~980ms. If i switch the scheduler flag to thread_packer_v2, p95 drops back under 120ms.
jonathan: nice. any logs for kernel selector decisions?
erika: enabling debug shows many small-batches being merged into oversized packed batches that then stall on a slow kernel path for quantized layers. long-tail comes from waiting for large pack formation.
max: short-term mitigations: 1) temporary rollback to v2.14 (pin variant) 2) route heavy-seq tenants to previous variant via routing policy 3) flip thread_packer flag off in config for v2.15 image (hotpatch) 4) increase runtime.service_min_replicas to reduce queueing. Which one should we do first?
priya: I'd prefer routing + hotpatch. rollback is fine but more disruptive for new fixes. hotpatching config is quickest.
jonathan: I can push a hotpatch to v2.15 to set thread_packer=thread_packer_v2 (safe toggle). will do canary 5% then 50% if green.
erika: thanks. support: please notify customers with short note: we're rolling a targeted config hotpatch to improve latency for medium-length requests, ETA 15m.
deploy-bot: deploy started for runtime v2.15 (hotpatch-thread_packer_v2) -> canary 5% @ 1719000180
max: monitoring dashboards show p95 starting to drop on canary cohort. hold for 10m then scale to 50%.
deploy-bot: canary looks good -> rolling to 50% @ 1719000280
priya: after 50% rollout p95 across prod cohorts trending back to baseline. I'll keep an eye on auth-cache misses (we saw slight uptick during the swap).
erika: follow-ups: - jonathan to complete hotpatch rollout and file runtime-issue with kernel packing telemetry - priya to run systematic synth test across seq lengths and update the packer heuristics RFC - max to update incident notes and notify affected customers - support to send update email when fully rolled.
jonathan: filing issue: https://redwood-internal/issue/INF-4821 (includes trace snippets and repro).
erika: thanks all, re-open if it resurfaces. :thumbsup:
